diagnostic_evidence.quote: A countable family $\{\varphi_j\}_{j=1}^{\infty} \subset L^{2}(P_X)$ is \emph{complete} in $L^{2}(P_X)$ if its linear span is dense in $L^{2}(P_X)$
Theorem~\ref{thm:cmean} guarantees $m \in L^{2}(P_X)$, so the relevant approximation question is whether $\{\varphi_j\}$ is dense in $L^{2}(P_X)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Definition 3.1 requires density of the span in L^{2}(P_X) for the actual P_X, but only the radial-basis families are qualified. The unqualified polynomial claim is false: for a moment-indeterminate P_X (e.g. a lognormal law) a Stieltjes class produces a nonzero bounded f in L^{2}(P_X) orthogonal to every polynomial, so the polynomial span is not dense. A countable Fourier system fails too (P_X = (delta_0+delta_1)/2 with f(0)=1, f(1)=-1 is orthogonal to every e^{2 pi i n x}). Completeness of these families needs hypotheses on P_X (e.g. compact support/moment determinacy, and support inside one period for a Fourier system).

failure_location.quote: Polynomial bases, Fourier bases, wavelet bases, and---under additional hypotheses on $P_X$---Gaussian or sigmoidal radial basis functions are complete \cite{steinwart2001influence}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Attach to the polynomial and Fourier/wavelet families the conditions actually needed (P_X compactly supported or moment-determinate; supported within one period for a Fourier system), as is already done for the radial-basis families.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that polynomial, Fourier or wavelet expansions can approximate E[Y|X] arbitrarily well in L^{2}(P_X), and hence that such fitting bases can drive the fit to the conditional mean, holds only for restricted P_X; the paper's examples (uniform P_X) are unaffected.
issues.title: Completeness of polynomial/Fourier/wavelet bases asserted without conditions on P_X
issues.why_classification: A one-clause restriction to standard support/determinacy conditions restores the claim, with no change to the method, the examples or any conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: training residuals may be artificially orthogonal to the features used during fitting, whereas independent diagnostic residuals can reveal structure that the fitted model has not captured.
in-basis checks therefore carry almost no information about whether $\hat f_n\approx m$
These conditions license reading $\hat\sigma_r^2$ as the estimated aleatoric floor $\E[\Var(Y\mid X)]$.

issues.failure_explanation: Step 2 probes only directions outside the fitted span, so the in-span component of the approximation gap E[(m(X)-f_n(X))^2] (the estimation error of the fitted coefficients) is never measured. On the very independent diagnostic set the procedure mandates, in-span probes do carry that signal: for psi in the fitted span, E[r psi] = <m - f_n, psi>, nonzero whenever the fit misses the population projection. The stated justification (OLS normal equations make the training residual orthogonal to the fitted features) applies to training residuals only and is contradicted by the paper's own Section 2 statement quoted above. Hence a fit far from E[Y|X] inside its own span passes every probe while sigma_r^2 exceeds the floor by the undetected in-span gap.

failure_location.quote: for every $\psi$ in the current family whose total degree exceeds that of the fitted basis

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Evaluate in-span as well as out-of-span probes on the independent diagnostic set and delete the training-residual rationale; the same effect-size rule then covers the estimation-error directions with no further argument.
issues.overall_effect: The Step-3 guarantee that the conditions license reading sigma_r^2 as the aleatoric floor, and the claim that the probe family certifies f_n approx m, are unsupported; Regime II/III verdicts and the floor estimates of Sections 6.1-6.2 carry an undetected in-span bias.
issues.title: Diagnostic blind spot: in-basis directions are never probed
issues.why_classification: A local change of the probe set in Step 2 plus one rationale sentence preserves the procedure, its tolerances and every reported conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The two questions are binary---reducible structure either is or is not detected, and the residual either is or is not within the task's tolerance---so together they partition the possibilities into four cases, shown in Table~\ref{tab:regimes}.

issues.failure_explanation: The stop rule states the criterion twice and inequivalently: 'no probe is both significant and practically large' is weaker than the stated operational form max_psi e_n(psi) <= epsilon, and the two disagree exactly when some probe has e_n > epsilon but is not significant (an under-powered diagnostic set). Table 1's rows are labelled by 'some psi: t_n significant, e_n>epsilon' and 'all psi: e_n<=epsilon', which are not complements, so the advertised four-case partition omits this case and prescribes no action for it; in that case the two criteria give opposite stopping verdicts, precisely the 'stop enlarging the deterministic model' decision the text calls the dangerous one.

failure_location.quote: declare the barrier reached when no out-of-basis probe is both significant \emph{and} practically large---operationally, when $\max_\psi e_n(\psi)\le\varepsilon$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix one criterion (no probe with e_n > epsilon, as the text's own prescription that epsilon decides what is large enough requires), use significance only to flag directions, and relabel the table rows as complements ('some psi: e_n>epsilon' / 'all psi: e_n<=epsilon').
issues.overall_effect: The decision rule is not total and its two formulations can return opposite barrier verdicts; the four regimes of tab:regimes do not partition the possibilities the text claims they cover.
issues.title: Inconsistent detection criterion; the four-regime split is not exhaustive
issues.why_classification: Harmonizing the criterion and the two row labels is a local wording repair that makes the split exhaustive and leaves the method and all conclusions intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Step~3 guards against it by phrasing the barrier as an \emph{equivalence}-style statement (no out-of-basis direction removes more than $\varepsilon$ of the residual variance)
the population residual mean-square is the floor $\E[\Var(Y\mid X)]$ plus the non-negative approximation gap $\E[(m(X)-\hat f_n(X))^2]$
the same probe family that certifies $\hat f_n\approx m$ also turns the observed residual variance into an estimate of the floor

issues.failure_explanation: Reading sigma_r^2 as the floor requires the whole gap E[(m-f_n)^2] to be negligible, but the stop rule bounds only each residual-probe projection separately. For an orthonormal probe family {psi_k}, e_n(psi_k) = E[r psi_k]^2/E[r^2] and the out-of-span gap is (sum_k e_n(psi_k)) E[r^2], so max_k e_n <= epsilon imposes no bound on the sum. Concrete case: X uniform on {-1,1}^N, Y = sum_k X_k + xi with Var(xi|X)=1 and a constant fit f_n = 0. Every probe psi_k = X_k has e_n = 1/(N+1) <= epsilon = 0.01 and is significant for large n, yet the gap is N against the floor 1 (sigma_r^2 = N+1); for N = 200 the diagnostic declares the barrier at an estimator wrong by a factor of 201. The second stop condition cannot help as written: enriching the probe families of Step 1 does not change sigma_r^2 at all.

failure_location.quote: These conditions license reading $\hat\sigma_r^2$ as the estimated aleatoric floor $\E[\Var(Y\mid X)]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the per-direction maximum by a bound on the aggregate out-of-span projection (e.g. sum_k e_n(psi_k) over an orthonormalized probe basis, or the R^2 of the residual on the whole probe span) and recompute the diagnostic curves of both demonstrations; the tolerance semantics and the barrier message survive.
issues.overall_effect: The licensing guarantee of Step 3 fails: sigma_r^2 may overestimate E[Var(Y|X)] by an arbitrarily large factor while the diagnostic passes, so the Regime II/III verdicts and the floor estimates reported in Sections 6.1-6.2 are not certified by the stated rule.
issues.title: Per-direction effect-size bound does not certify the aleatoric floor
issues.why_classification: Restoring the guarantee requires changing the operative statistic of the stop rule and re-optimizing/recomputing the reported diagnostics in both demonstrations: a contained but nontrivial change beyond a local edit, though the framework and its message remain recognizably intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Both $\theta$-dependent terms in \eqref{eq:vs-decomp} are non-negative, so the minimizer drives each to zero.
Let $g_\theta \colon \X \times \mathcal{Z} \to \R$ be measurable and square-integrable for each $\theta$

issues.failure_explanation: The decomposition is correct, but the collapse conclusion does not follow. Non-negativity only gives L(theta) >= E[Var(Y|X)] with equality iff both theta-dependent terms vanish; the minimizer forces them to zero only if the family contains a Z-independent element equal to E[Y|X] and the infimum is attained. 'Sufficiently expressive' is undefined and implies neither: for the legitimate family g(x,z) = f(x) + z with f ranging over all square-integrable functions of x (unrestricted in x), the unique minimizer f = E[Y|X] has Var_Z(g) = 1, contradicting the stated conclusion. The last proof inference is therefore invalid without an expressivity/attainment hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: In particular, the minimizer over $\theta$, taken over a sufficiently expressive family, satisfies $\E_Z[g_\theta(X, Z)] = \E[Y \mid X]$ almost surely and $\Var_Z(g_\theta(X, Z)) = 0$ almost surely.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'taken over a sufficiently expressive family' by a precise hypothesis (the family contains x -> E[Y|X] independent of z and L attains its infimum) and derive the collapse from attaining the lower bound E[Var(Y|X)]; the decomposition and all intended applications are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The headline collapse statement of the proposition (and the abstract/introduction claims that injecting latent randomness collapses a squared-loss predictor to the conditional mean) is false for the stated class of square-integrable g_theta; it holds only for families that can represent E[Y|X] deterministically and attain the infimum.
issues.title: Variance-suppression conclusion needs a precise expressivity/attainment hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding the missing hypothesis and adjusting the last proof sentence is a short local repair that preserves the proposition, its decomposition and every application (including the affine latent model of Section 6.1).
